transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2028-12-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rafael Gomez (Redwood SE), Priya Nambiar (Alcyon - Head of ML), Evan Lowe (Alcyon - Platform Eng), Marta Ruiz (Alcyon - CTO)

Summary (auto): quick alignment on constraints, heavy emphasis on context length and security; customer leans toward private for sensitive pipeline but wants hosted perf baseline; agreed on pilot and benchmark plan.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining uh on a Friday, really appreciate it. Quick intro round, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Rafael is our systems SE, he'll jump into perf and deploys. Priya?
[00:10] Priya Nambiar: Hi, yeah thanks Maya. Priya Nambiar, head of ML at Alcyon. We're looking at models to power a developer-facing code assist and internal knowledge Q&A. A bunch of sensitive docs so security's a big deal.
[00:21] Evan Lowe: Evan, platform. We'll own infra and network. We're curious about VPC and private options.
[00:26] Marta Ruiz: Marta, CTO, here to make sure roadmap aligns with cost and timelines.
[00:31] Rafael Gomez: Great. Quick agenda — model choices (open models mainly), context length needs, multilingual, tool calling for internal APIs, and deployment paths (hosted/dedicated/private). Sound right?
[00:41] All: yeah / yep

[00:48] Priya: So to kick off — context. Our main use case is a chat assistant that needs 30 to 60k token context for long doc summarization and chain-of-thought traces. We also have multi-lingual customer support — English Spanish French German primarily. Latency requirement is soft for async but token cost matters.
[01:10] Rafael: Understood. When you say 30–60k, is that active generation context or retrieval-augmented combined context? Do you plan to store full doc in the prompt or use KV cache / retrieval?
[01:22] Priya: A mix. We'll retrieve chunks and sometimes stream long user histories plus docs. We want the option to feed a lot of context to reduce hallucinations for multi-document answers.
[01:34] Rafael: Okay, so we should look at models that have native longer context windows or can be extended via Redwood's runtime KV-cache and stitching. There's a few open variants — LlamaX-64k (we'll be careful with names, might be Llama-2-64k forks), Mistral Long, and some specialized long-context M-weights. Tradeoffs: performance & token cost.

[01:58] Evan: How does Redwood handle quantization and memory footprint for 64k contexts? We have limited GPU RAM in Private.
[02:06] Rafael: Good question. For dedicated/private we recommend 4-bit quant profiles for many workloads, but 64k context pushes memory on the runtime side because of KV-cache growth. We do kernel selection to optimize attention, and for very long contexts we can offload part of the KV to host RAM if you accept some latency bump. In Hosted we operate optimized kernels across our fleet and can agg batch to keep costs down.
[02:32] Priya: Hmm, that offload — is that configurable per-deployment? We have a strict SLA on p99 latency for interactive support.
[02:41] Rafael: Yes, you can set routing policies and cache retention thresholds. For p99 you might want Dedicated with reserved capacity so we can tune batch windows and avoid noisy neighbor effects.

[02:55] Marta: Security — we need SOC2, SSO with SAML, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs retained for 12 months. Also data residency in EU for a subset of customers. How does Redwood support that?
[03:08] Maya: We have SOC2 and can provide the report. Private deployment offers VPC and on-prem, plus KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM options) and audit logs. For Hosted we have EU regions and encrypted-at-rest, but some customers with strict residency prefer Private.
[03:24] Priya: Ok makes sense. We might run the pilot on Hosted to compare perf & then move to Private for production if security gating requires it.

[03:33] Evan: Tool-calling — we need the model to call internal APIs for account lookups and to run code execution safely. We also plan to do structured output from the model. How robust is Redwood's function-calling / tool integration?
[03:45] Rafael: We support function/tool calling patterns, streaming function call tokens, and typed structured outputs. SE note: you can register tools in the runtime, set allowed scopes, and we have sandboxing for tool execution in private deployments. There are safety policies — rate limits and allow-lists.
[04:03] Priya: Is there an SDK or connector for our existing internal graph API?
[04:07] Rafael: Yep, SDKs in Python/Go/Node, we can show sample code. For private you'll run the agent connector inside your network so calls never leave VPC.

[04:18] Marta: Cost — we need to compare hosted per-token vs dedicated reserved pricing. Also we'd like to see impact of context length on cost per request.
[04:27] Maya: We'll send a pricing grid. Quick note: 64k context significantly increases token charge because tokens are both input and output — also cache hits can reduce costs if you reuse prefixes. Redwood Optimize can recommend quant/profile and batching to reduce unit cost.

[04:44] Priya: On models — we want open models primarily due to licensing and ability to run in private. Any recommendations for best accuracy at 32k vs 64k?
[04:55] Rafael: For 32k there are a few good open models: Mistral-Slim-32k variants, Falcon-40B-32k forks, and some community 34B-32k tuned weights. For >32k, the choices narrow — some groups provide 64k context variants but often with accuracy tradeoffs. Another approach is progressive retrieval + reranking so you rarely need the full 64k in the active attention window.
[05:18] Evan: Curious about multilingual tokenization differences — Spanish and German compound words blow up token counts.
[05:24] Rafael: Yes tokenization differences matter; we recommend testing with your real traffic. Redwood's eval harness can run tokenization profiles and simulate cost. For German compounding you may see +10–30% token expansion depending on tokenizer.

[05:40] Priya: Benchmarks — we want to run A/B between hosted Redwood-backed Mistral-Long-64k (if available) vs dedicated Falco-32k quant3 and maybe a private custom fine-tuned model. Can Redwood run that?
[05:52] Maya: Absolutely. Typical pilot is a 2–4 week bench: we run perf (latency, tokens/sec), quality (ROUGE/BERTScore on your eval prompts), and cost projection. For Private we'll mirror the runtime as close as possible but you'll want to provision GPUs to match.

[06:10] Marta: Timeline — we want a decision in Q1 and possibly a pilot starting early Jan. Any blockers from your side?
[06:17] Maya: No blockers. We'll get the security pack and pricing by Friday, Rafael will propose a benchmark runbook by next week, and we can schedule the bench the week of Jan 8th.

[06:28] Priya: One nit — how do you handle model rollouts and version pinning? We need reproducibility for regulatory reasons.
[06:34] Rafael: We support model version pinning, can pin weights + runtime config, rollouts (canary/A-B), and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. Also audit trails for which model served each token.

[06:47] Evan: For Private, what's the minimum GPU footprint you'd advise for 64k contexts? We run mostly A100 80GB.
[06:55] Rafael: A100 80GB is a good baseline. For 64k you'll likely need multi-GPU sharded setup unless you use offload. Our recommended starting cluster is 2x80GB or 4x80GB depending on model size; Rafael note: if you use quant4 and kernel optimizations you might fit some 34B long-context models on 2x80GB.

[07:14] Priya: Regarding hallucinations — is there a recommended practice for tool-chain to reduce them? We plan to use retrieval + reranking + system prompts.
[07:22] Rafael: That's the pattern we see works best. Also use guardrails — post-call rejection heuristics, and stop sequences. Redwood Optimize can monitor quality regressions on eval sets and alert.

[07:35] (brief crosstalk)
[07:37] Marta: One more thing — data residency. If some EU customers want all PII to remain in EU, can we do hybrid between Hosted EU for public users and Private for enterprise?
[07:46] Maya: Yes hybrid is possible; smart routing can send EU requests to EU-hosted or your Private nodes in EU. We can document that.

[07:55] Evan: Any gotchas with SAML and provisioning for Private control plane?
[07:59] Rafael: Private control plane integrates with your SAML IdP and supports RBAC. For on-prem there's an initial install window we'll coordinate. We'll also provide automation via Terraform modules for infra setup.

[08:12] Priya: Are there example benchmarks you can share for long-context models? We want to see p50/p95/p99 numbers.
[08:18] Rafael: We'll attach a benchmark sheet. Quick verbal: Hosted 32k models often have p50 ~80–150ms per token pop for some optimized models; 64k can add 20–80% latency depending on offload strategy.

[08:34] (silence)
[08:36] Priya: Ok this is helpful. Let's call out explicit next steps.

[08:40] Maya: Great — I'll summarize: 1) Redwood to send pricing/security pack by 12/22, 2) Rafael to send benchmark runbook & sample infra scripts by 12/29, 3) Alcyon to send redacted sample logs and evaluation prompts by 12/27, 4) schedule perf bench week of Jan 8. Anything to add?
[08:58] Priya: Also can you include tokenization profile for German/spanish and an estimate for token inflation?
[09:03] Rafael: Yes, will include tokenization report and expected token delta per language.

[09:09] Marta: Ok, thanks everyone.
[09:11] Maya: Thanks team. We'll follow up in email with the artifacts.

[09:15] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: some words may be mis-transcribed (e.g., 'K-V cash' for KV cache, 'quantisization' for quantization) and model names are approximate references to community variants. References to internal docs and decks will be shared as links in follow-up.
